units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 16b:12">B. Kam. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>בני ת׳</he> tamed animals.
Ib. ארי ת׳ a tamed lion.—Esp. ת׳ רעה bad manners, depravity; degenerate child.
<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 10:8">Nidd. X, 8</cite> <he>הרי זו ת׳ ר׳</he> this is mischievous conduct.
<cite ref="Chagigah 15a:8">Ḥag. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>לאחר שיצא לת׳ ר׳</he> after he (Elisha ben Abuya) had become an infidel.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1:1">Ex. R. s. 1</cite>, beg (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 21:11">Gen. XXI, 11</cite>) <he>על שיצא לת׳ ר׳</he> (Abraham was displeased because of his son) because of his depravity.
<cite ref="Genesis 21:11">Ib.</cite> <he>כל המונע … סוף בא ת׳ ר׳</he> when a man refrains from chastising his son, the latter will in the end turn to mischief.
<cite ref="Genesis 21:11">Ib.</cite> <he>ללמוד ממנו ת׳ ר׳</he> to learn bad manner from him.
<cite ref="Genesis 21:11">Ib.</cite> <he>קשה ת׳ ר׳ בתוך ביתו וכ׳</he> a degenerate child in a man’s house is worse than the war of Gog and Magog.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 28">Gen. R. s. 28</cite> <he>למלך … והוציאו לת׳ ר׳</he> a king that gave his son in charge of a pedagogue, and he led him to a bad life; a. fr.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:3:24">Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="V00291"><he>תּוֹרִיב</he></cite>.
